subject: NovaHealth pilot - SCCs / UK addendum and TIA routing clarification
messages:
From: Sarah Black <sarah.black@novahealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: NovaHealth Legal <legal@novahealth.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot data flows / transfer mechanisms question

Hi Priyom,

We're getting ready to kick off the NovaHealth pilot with Redwood and legal has a couple of quick questions about cross-border protections. Specifically: which transfer mechanism will Redwood rely on for EU->US and UK->US traffic (SCCs + UK IDTA/UK Addendum by default?), and what evidence can you provide for on-prem / connector-based egress? Our security team also asked for a TIA scope so they can confirm logging/retention won't violate healthcare record rules.

Can you send over the current DPA, subprocessor list, and a short TIA scoping template we can review? Pilot target start 2028-03-01 so we'd appreciate anything this week.

Thanks,
Sarah Black
DPO | NovaHealth

Attachment: -- none --

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Black <sarah.black@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flows / transfer mechanisms question

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and timeline. Short answers up front:

- Transfer mechanisms: For EU data we use the EU SCCs (latest version) by default; for UK-origin data we apply the UK IDTA + Redwood UK Addendum where requested.
- Evidence: we can supply the executed DPA, the current subprocessor inventory, and a TIA scoping template. For connector-based egress we have a short evidence pack showing egress paths and whether data leaves the EU/UK boundary.

I'm attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, Subprocessor_List_202802.pdf, and TIA_Scoping_Template.xlsx.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether NovaHealth classifies the pilot data as "pseudonymized PHI" or "identifiable health data"? That will change recommended retention and logging controls. Also confirm region(s) (EU only vs EU+UK). If you want, we can include a fallback routing policy to keep traffic within EU-only regions for the pilot.

I'll loop in Kimberly from Security for TIA detail. If we can get answers by 02/18 we should be able to finalize evidence before your 03/01 pilot start.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (DPA, v3), Subprocessor_List_202802.pdf (inventory), TIA_Scoping_Template.xlsx (scoping checklist)

Subject: Re: Pilot data flows / transfer mechanisms question (internal)

Internal notes for the thread before we respond to NovaHealth:

- If NovaHealth calls the data "identifiable health data" we should tighten retention and consider recommending an EU-only routing profile for the pilot.
- Flag: they mentioned an on-prem connector. Need to confirm if the connector pushes logs to our hosted collectors or keeps logs local. That affects TIA scope (esp. egress & encryption-in-transit).
- We should pre-populate the TIA scoping template with the minimal set of questions:
  * Data categories and examples (PHI, pseudonymized PHI, other PII)
  * Ingress/egress points and whether the connector performs transformation
  * Retention policy desired for logs and app-level data (days)
  * Any subprocessor endpoints in non-EU/UK regions (e.g., CloudVault Inc. in US)
- Marissa: can you check whether we have a precedent DPA exception for 3rd-party telemetry for healthcare customers?

I'll draft a short response to Sarah that includes the TIA questions and our suggested fallback (EU-only) routing + brief note about SCCs/UK IDTA.

-Kim
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot data flows / transfer mechanisms question

Hi Sarah — following up with the TIA scoping questions (pasted below) and our suggested interim controls for the pilot. If you can answer the bullets below we will confirm the appropriate transfer mechanism and prepare the evidence pack.

TIA scoping questions (please fill or mark N/A):
1) Pilot region(s): EU-only / UK-only / EU+UK / other — please specify countries.
2) Data categories: identify whether records include direct patient identifiers, pseudonymized PHI, or only aggregated analytics. Examples are helpful.
3) Connector details: is the connector (a) on-prem, (b) hosted by NovaHealth in your cloud, or (c) a Redwood-managed connector? Does it perform any transformation (hashing, tokenization) before sending?
4) Logging/retention: desired retention for request logs and application-level logs (days). Any legal hold expectations?
5) Subprocessors: confirm any subprocessors you expect to use (e.g., CloudVault Inc. for storage). We will map against our Subprocessor_List_202802.pdf and note any overlapping processors.
6) Export/Export exceptions: any regulatory constraints that require data to stay in-country or additional safeguards?

Suggested pilot controls (we can implement quickly):
- EU-only routing policy for the pilot (recommended if data is identifiable).
- Token-level pseudonymization option before egress (if connector supports it).
- Short-term retention profile: 30 days for logs, unless you require otherwise.

We'll produce: executed DPA (attached), subprocessor inventory, and a short evidence note showing routing and the path for connector egress. If you confirm region + data type by 02/20 we can get the TIA evidence to you by 02/25.

Link to TIA scoping form: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/NovaHealth/TIA-scoping-2028-02.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

From: Sarah Black <sarah.black@novahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Legal <legal@novahealth.com>
Date: 2028-02-22T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flows / transfer mechanisms question

Hi Priyom — sorry for the delay, answers below: 

1) Regions: EU+UK (primary data centers in Ireland and London).
2) Data categories: pseudonymized PHI for the pilot (IDs removed, but linkable via a local private key).
3) Connector: on-prem agent that pushes encrypted payloads to Redwood ingestion endpoints; agent performs AES-256 encryption but does not tokenise.
4) Logging/retention: NovaHealth prefers 90-day request-log retention for troubleshooting but can accept 30 days for pilot if legally necessary; app-level retention is 180 days. No active legal holds for pilot.
5) Subprocessors: we will use CloudVault Inc. (storage) and TelemetryOps Ltd (logging); both are US-based.
6) Export constraints: none beyond normal healthcare regulatory obligations; we do require UK addendum for UK-subject data.

We'll sign the DPA with the UK Addendum included and prefer the EU+UK routing with explicit note about CloudVault being a subprocessor. Please provide the final evidence pack and an updated subprocessor map that highlights any US-based subprocessors used in the pilot.

DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-docs/na-7421

Thanks,
Sarah Black
DPO | NovaHealth
